disclaimer: General educational information only. It does not list doses and is not a recommendation to start, change or stop any medicine. Medicines for mental health must be prescribed and monitored by a doctor. Never stop a prescribed medicine suddenly without talking to your prescriber. Content should be reviewed by a pharmacist or psychiatrist before public launch and checked against your national medicines authority (e.g. Fimea in Finland).

classes.name: SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors)
classes.howItWorks: Raise the availability of serotonin, a chemical messenger involved in mood and anxiety regulation.
classes.whatToExpect: Usually need 2-6 weeks for full effect. Early side effects often fade within the first weeks.
importantWarnings: In people under 25, tell your doctor right away if suicidal thoughts or agitation increase early in treatment.
Do not stop suddenly. Discontinuation symptoms (dizziness, 'electric' sensations, irritability) can occur.

Risk of serotonin syndrome when combined with some medicines or supplements (for example St John's wort, tramadol, triptans, MAO inhibitors). Always tell prescribers and pharmacists everything you take.
Alcohol can worsen side effects and mood.

classes.name: SNRIs and other newer antidepressants
classes.howItWorks: Act on serotonin and noradrenaline (SNRIs), or on other receptors (mirtazapine, vortioxetine).
classes.whatToExpect: Similar timeline to SSRIs. Mirtazapine often helps sleep and appetite early on.
importantWarnings: Blood pressure may need checking with venlafaxine and duloxetine.
Stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms; venlafaxine is particularly known for this.
Same interaction cautions as SSRIs.

classes.name: Benzodiazepines
usedFor: Short-term relief of severe anxiety or acute agitation
classes.howItWorks: Enhance the calming GABA system in the brain, giving fast but temporary relief.
classes.whatToExpect: Work within an hour but do not treat the cause of anxiety. Intended for short periods only.
importantWarnings: Tolerance and dependence can develop, sometimes within weeks.
Dangerous together with alcohol or opioids (risk of breathing problems).
Can impair driving and machine use.
Stopping after regular use should be gradual and supervised.

classes.name: Hydroxyzine and other sedating antihistamines
classes.howItWorks: An antihistamine with a calming, sedating effect.
classes.whatToExpect: Fast acting; not habit-forming in the same way as benzodiazepines, but intended for limited use.
importantWarnings: Can affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation) in some people. Tell your doctor about heart conditions or other medicines affecting heart rhythm.
Avoid alcohol, and be careful driving.
Older adults are more sensitive to side effects.

classes.name: Beta-blockers (for physical anxiety symptoms)
usedFor: Physical symptoms of performance anxiety such as shaking and racing heart (a doctor decides if suitable)
classes.howItWorks: Block adrenaline effects on the heart and body; they do not change worrying thoughts.
classes.whatToExpect: Used as needed or short-term in selected cases.
importantWarnings: Not suitable for people with asthma or certain heart conditions.
Can hide warning signs of low blood sugar in people with diabetes.

classes.name: Mood stabilisers
usedFor: Bipolar disorder (prevention of mania and depression)
classes.howItWorks: Reduce the extremes of mood swings by several mechanisms.
classes.whatToExpect: Long-term treatment under specialist care with regular check-ups.
importantWarnings: Lithium requires regular blood tests; dehydration, some painkillers (NSAIDs) and some blood-pressure medicines can raise lithium levels dangerously.
Valproate must not be used in pregnancy unless there is no alternative; discuss contraception with your doctor.
Lamotrigine: stop and seek urgent care if a new skin rash appears.

classes.name: Antipsychotics
usedFor: Added to antidepressants in some treatment-resistant depression
classes.howItWorks: Mainly affect dopamine (and other) signalling to reduce hallucinations, delusions and severe agitation.
classes.whatToExpect: Started and adjusted by a psychiatrist; monitoring of weight, blood sugar and cholesterol is usual.
importantWarnings: Metabolic changes (weight, blood sugar, cholesterol) should be monitored.
Do not stop suddenly, since symptoms can return or worsen.

classes.name: 'Z-drugs' and sleeping tablets
classes.howItWorks: Act on the same calming system as benzodiazepines.
classes.whatToExpect: Meant for short use (days to a couple of weeks). Habits and therapy (CBT-I) work better in the long term.
importantWarnings: Can cause sleepwalking or other complex behaviours while not fully awake.
Dependence and tolerance may develop.
Do not combine with alcohol.

generalSafety: Tell every prescriber and pharmacist about all medicines, supplements and herbal products you use.
Do not share medicines or use someone else's prescription.
Take medicines as prescribed. If side effects bother you, call your doctor before stopping.
In pregnancy or breastfeeding, always discuss any medicine with your doctor first.
If you have thoughts of harming yourself at any time on a medicine, seek help immediately.
